gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Loud, cheerful, bent like cable. Luckiest Guy handles the shouting, while Noto Sans Tirhuta, with its big-gapped terminals and dominant x-height, does the quiet sans-serif work underneath.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Noto Sans Ugaritic reads friendly and low-slung, its letter mouths left open like unjoined chalk arcs. Luckiest Guy brings the wire-like, tubular shouting; Noto Sans Ugaritic is the one that keeps sentences moving.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-vai: Cheerful and loud, drawn with a single nib. Noto Sans Vai sits beneath it as a plain sans whose words settle into solid blocks, giving the heading's bounce something steady to lean on.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Luckiest Guy looks like neon tube bent into letters, every stroke the same glowing thickness. Noto Sans Vithkuqi follows with open throats and a barely-there step from capital to lowercase, so a long stretch of sans-serif text flows smoothly.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Luckiest Guy draws every stroke with no thick-to-thin variation, a loud, cheerful, tightly poured line of ink. Noto Sans Wancho reads smooth and sturdy.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-warang-cit: Cheerful and brash, Luckiest Guy sets down a plain stripe of constant ink with its mean line high. Noto Sans Warang Citi calms it into solid blocks.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-yi: Loud, jolly letters outlined in one steady thickness, with the mean line set high. Give Noto Sans Yi a little extra size, since its deep lowercase and open rounds hold up well.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-: Luckiest Guy cuts its letters like sign-shop vinyl at a single line width, loud and cheerful. And Noto Sans Zanabazar Square, with its soaring x-height and wide gaps, picks up the quieter sans text beneath.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-traditional-nus: Noto Traditional Nushu moves like a broad-nibbed pen that never curls shut. Its bowls fill the line, so long paragraphs under Luckiest Guy feel friendly and unhurried.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-numans: Luckiest Guy gives every stroke a pipe-like body, cheerful and loud with the mean line set high. Numans spreads its swollen lowercase wide with generous tracking, so a long passage drifts along slowly and easily.
